title: I Let the RV Dump-Station Queue Catch the Owner Who Cut the Line

parts.text: I pulled hose 2 at 8:41 a.m. and owner Brant had already dropped in from the exit lane. The sign said: ENTER WITH THE ARROW. ONE HOSE. NO EXIT CUTS. I was forty-eight, renter, holding a dump ticket. Brant shrugged. "Owners are the lane." I photographed the sign, the ticket, and his hose on my number. Then I asked for the station log. At 8:47 the attendant pinged why Brant's name was on an exit cut. I kept my voice indoor and let the timestamp talk. I have learned the difference between a title and a line item.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The attendant can see Brant's exit-lane cut on hose 2 during my dump.

social.video_title: The owner cut the dump-station line from the exit — Part 1/2
social.description: RV dump, an arrow sign, a hose on my number. I logged the cut. Would you have asked the attendant?

parts.text: Brant called it efficiency until the attendant asked for the still. I printed the log, the sign, and the ticket. He reentered with the arrow. Brant dumped in order and told the next owner efficiency was always about optics. Optics is a word owners use when arrows exist. Queue now has a second line: EXIT IS NOT ENTRY. I keep hose 2. Brant brown-bags the jokes. The pad finally looks like a ticket, not a shortcut. If it is written, it can be applied to the person who wrote it.

social.description: Station log, arrow reentry, and a second line. Was efficiency ever the exit?
